thread.title: China Executes Four Canadians Amid Drug-Related Charges
thread.title_full: China Executes Four Canadians Amid Drug-Related Charges

author: ROB GILLIES
title: China Executes Four Canadians Amid Drug-Related Charges
text:
• China executed four Canadians in recent months, according to Canada's Foreign Minister Mélanie Joly.
• The executions were related to drug crimes, as stated by Beijing's embassy in Ottawa.
• China does not recognize dual citizenship, which affected the cases of the executed individuals.
• Joly and former Prime Minister Justin Trudeau requested clemency for the dual citizens involved.
• The identities of the executed individuals have not been disclosed at the request of their families.
• Global Affairs Canada continues to provide consular assistance to the families of the executed.
• Canada is advocating for clemency for Robert Schellenberg, a Canadian sentenced to death for drug smuggling.
• China imposes severe penalties for drug-related crimes, according to a spokesperson for the Chinese embassy.
• China is believed to execute more prisoners annually than the rest of the world combined, though exact figures are a state secret.
• Executions in China are traditionally carried out by gunshot, with lethal injections also being used.
• Tensions between Canada and China have escalated, with retaliatory tariffs imposed by both countries.
• China is Canada's second-largest trading partner, but relations have soured since the 2018 arrest of a Huawei executive in Canada.
• Amnesty International condemned the executions, stating they are shocking and inhumane.
• The head of Amnesty International for English-speaking Canada called the executions a wake-up call for Canada.
